headline: Florida's education and workforce pathways.
summary: Selected public-university bachelor's programs, observed graduate outcomes, and long-term occupational projections. The report periods are historical benchmarks, not current hiring estimates.
coverageNote: The selected programs exclude state-college, private, certificate, graduate, migration, and adjacent-occupation supply. Graduate-to-opening ratios describe limited coverage, not a labor shortage or surplus. Florida employment matches exclude some employment outside the covered administrative records and cannot establish total employment or retention.
methodology: Demand uses Florida 2022-32 long-term occupational projections published through O*NET OnLine from Projections Central; openings include growth and replacement.
FETPIP's 2023-24 university graduate report remained the latest posted on September 10, 2026. Employment percentages refer to matches in covered Florida records, not all employment.
The coverage proxy divides covered bachelor's graduates by projected annual openings. It sizes a visible pipeline; it does not label a shortage or surplus.
Institution leaders are the three largest disclosed producers in the selected FETPIP program; suppressed values remain unavailable.
Project pressure links only to named records in the Floridanomics project capex ledger and is not a complete hiring forecast.

clusters.label: AI & Software
clusters.question: How does the selected ai & software pathway relate to projected occupational demand?
clusters.read: The 2023-24 cohort includes 2,262 graduates in the selected program. FETPIP matches 40% to full-time Florida employment in its follow-up records. The occupation's 7,330 projected annual openings cover 2022-32 and include growth and replacement needs. These are different populations and periods.
